one_line: Local confidential-document analysis with identity-preserving redaction for agents.
what_it_does: Parses documents in-page, detects identifying values, lets the user control disclosure, and exposes structured analysis/decode tools.
leverage_rationale: In-page structured tools and stable redaction tokens make privacy-preserving document reasoning substantially more reliable than a general agent reading the UI or raw file.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description state the agent never receives names, account numbers, or addresses.
Stable tokens preserve cross-document identity relationships while withholding identities.
Frame sheet shows document review alongside detected/highlighted confidential values and structured output.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent local parsing, review, agent-analysis, and decode workflow, though the visual evidence does not show a complete agent invocation trace.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive.
Frames show landing, document opening, and analysis/review states.
Description covers TXT, MD, PDF, DOCX and per-value disclosure controls.
impact_rationale: Confidential contracts, patient records, and deals are a concrete audience and problem; local identity separation addresses a meaningful privacy barrier.
impact_evidence: Explicit use cases include client contracts and patient records.
Local processing and user-controlled disclosure are directly aligned to confidentiality needs.
creativity_rationale: The structural-versus-identity distinction and reversible stable-token workflow are an original, memorable approach to agent document analysis.
creativity_evidence: Stable identity tokens preserve reasoning relationships without exposing identities.
Withheld values have no reversible token.
usability_note: Review-before-disclosure is understandable, but the multi-step privacy workflow adds complexity.
red_flags: No public repository; no direct tool-call trace in the supplied frames.
Video transcript is only music and a brief utterance.
standouts: Privacy boundary is enforced at the page/tool surface rather than merely promised.
advance_reason: Strong privacy-centered WebMCP delta, concrete use case, and coherent demonstrated product flow.

Session Ledger and endSession behavior are specified.
impact_rationale: Marketers running creator campaigns have a real matching, compliance, and approval problem; the product directly targets it.
impact_evidence: KOC search and campaign deal proposal are a specific operational workflow.
Human approval for risky commitments addresses a credible trust need.
creativity_rationale: The combination of autonomy tiers, trust scoring, and policy-gated proposal execution is a fresh synthesis for campaign operations.
creativity_evidence: AEGIS trust score changes autonomy behavior.
Every proposal, block, rejection, correction, and confirmation is recorded.
usability_note: The staged workflow is clear, though the dashboard is dense.
red_flags: Frames do not visibly prove actual agent tool calls.
standouts: Safety controls are integrated into the mutation path, not added as a report afterward.

advance_reason: Strong agent-centered business workflow with unusually explicit policy and audit boundaries.

one_line: Agent-native accessibility audit and remediation studio with human approval and concurrency safety.
what_it_does: Inspects live accessibility state, stages ARIA fixes, shows diffs, validates epoch locks, and requires approval before destructive commits.
leverage_rationale: Structured live DOM introspection and guarded mutation are central; generic UI driving cannot comparably provide reliable accessibility-tree state, staged patches, and concurrency-bound commits.
leverage_evidence: Tools audit_accessibility_tree, stage_aria_remediation, and commit_a11y_fix are described.
Epoch locks prevent stale patches after user mutation.
Human approval is required before destructive mutation.
execution_rationale: The architecture is intentional and detailed, but the supplied frame is too small to verify actual audit findings or remediation end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and public repository available.
Description specifies introspection, diff staging, honeypots, locks, and authority boundaries.
Frame shows a structured dark studio UI, but no legible WCAG output.
impact_rationale: Accessibility remediation addresses a broad, concrete developer and end-user need, with safety features targeting real risks of automated DOM changes.
impact_evidence: Specific WCAG/ARIA and focus-trap problem is identified.
Product directly audits and remediates live DOM accessibility issues.
creativity_rationale: Combining agent-native accessibility inspection with adversarial honeypots, optimistic concurrency, and human authority boundaries is notably original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Adversarial honeypots defend against prompt injection/destructive mutation.
usability_note: IDE-style staging and diffs are promising, but the supplied visual evidence is not legible enough to judge workflow clarity.
red_flags: Frame sheet is too small to verify accessibility findings or fixes.
standouts: Strong safety model for agent write access to live DOM.
WebMCP is central to structured accessibility state and controlled mutation.
advance_reason: High-impact, highly WebMCP-specific developer workflow with strong safety design.

one_line: Agent-operated kerning workbench that visually evaluates pairs and exports fonts.
what_it_does: Surveys font pairs, returns rendered candidate comparisons to an agent, applies selected values, previews words, and exports TTF files.
leverage_rationale: The agent needs page-rendered visual evidence and an agent-only comparison tool; structured WebMCP exposes capabilities that generic UI driving cannot perform comparably reliably at scale.
leverage_evidence: Transcript reports 16 calls and 51 pairs processed in three minutes.
preview_pairs returns labelled rendered images rather than numbers.
Agent shares live font/canvas state and leaves already-correct pairs untouched.
execution_rationale: Transcript provides unusually strong end-to-end evidence from instruction through visual inspection, selective edits, word checks, and real font export.
execution_evidence: Video is 113 seconds with detailed transcript.
51 pairs processed, 46 changed and 5 left; second font had 10 changes and 41 untouched.
Transcript states export writes real GPOS and kern tables.
impact_rationale: Type designers face hundreds of subjective pair-spacing decisions; this can save substantial labor while preserving manual control.
impact_evidence: Transcript contrasts a week of manual work with minutes of agent-assisted processing.
Manual arrow-key editing and hover-before values preserve designer control.
creativity_rationale: Using rendered visual comparisons as the agent's decision substrate for subjective typography is a novel and deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Six of eight tools return images for visual judgment.
Agent-only preview_pairs creates candidate comparison sheets no UI button offers.
usability_note: The workflow is direct and retains hand editing, though kerning remains specialized.
standouts: Excellent visual evidence and transcript alignment.
WebMCP enables visual, stateful, high-volume typography work rather than merely clicking buttons.
advance_reason: Best-evidenced submission: transformative WebMCP leverage, complete workflow, and genuinely original visual-agent interaction.
